issues: What is the correct legal test and standard of proof for assessing an internal flight alternative (IFA) in a refugee appeal
Whether the tribunal applied too high a standard of proof in assessing the risk of being located by the agent of persecution in the proposed IFA location
Whether a claimant's sworn testimony is presumed truthful absent reasons to doubt it, and whether lack of corroboration alone can rebut that presumption
Whether the tribunal erred by giving little weight to a psychological report because it was based on a single non-treating assessment
Whether discrimination, hardship (cost of living, non-indigenous status) and mental health evidence were properly considered in assessing the reasonableness prong of the IFA test
What standard of review applies to a refugee appeal division's factual and mixed fact-law findings on judicial review
Whether the tribunal's treatment of corroborating evidence (husband's affidavit) and country condition evidence was reasonable
key_facts: Client fled a West African country with two young daughters to avoid FGM being imposed by her husband's extended family
She was accused of witchcraft by the family based on an oracle's pronouncement following a death in the family
The family reported her to police, who questioned her husband for about two hours about her whereabouts
No further police contact in the roughly ten months since the interrogation
Client alleges a husband's uncle with political campaign connections could locate her anywhere via personal influence and a national police computer network
Refugee Appeal Division found a viable internal flight alternative (IFA) in another major city far from her home region
Tribunal found her evidence about the uncle's reach thin and inconsistent, and noted the husband's short affidavit did not mention the uncle or the interrogation
Tribunal found discrimination against non-indigenous residents and high cost of living did not make the IFA unreasonable given her education and family business success
Tribunal gave little weight to a psychologist's report diagnosing depression and PTSD, based on a single one-hour assessment by a non-treating clinician
Client seeks judicial review challenging the standard of proof applied, the treatment of her sworn evidence, and treatment of mental health and country condition evidence
causes_of_action: Application for judicial review of a Refugee Appeal Division decision to the Federal Court
